confirmed.what_breaks: The quantity rule is neither the one ADR-007 decided nor pinned by a test: a planted defect widening the pattern survives, and a zero-padded value such as 000005 is refused although it is 5.

Input '000005': the original parseQuantity (:98) returns null and the form shows line.quantity.invalid; the mutant returns 5 and accepts the line, while '00005' passes both. ADR-007 line 15: quantity is trimmed text matching ^\d+$, then the range 1 to MAX_QUANTITY, so the mutant is closer to the decision than the code (COR-11, SEC-11, CON-11 report the same deviation). tests/validation.test.js:115-127 try '0', '10000', '2.0', '1e3', '-1', '', '+1', 'two' and never a six-digit zero-padded value; tests/validation.spec.mjs:210-216 neither. Fix: the ADR-007 pattern plus tests that '000005' is stored as 5 and '100000' is refused by the range.

confirmed.what_breaks: Above 2^46 cents a shown total can be one cent off although addLine accepts it as safe; a theoretical limit at about 70 trillion euros.
confirmed.evidence: format.js:8 divides cents by 100 in double precision. For cents = 9007199254740987 (safe, accepted by lines.js:21) the exact quotient 90071992547409.87 lies in [2^46, 2^47), where doubles are 1/64 apart: the nearest double is 90071992547409.875 and Intl.NumberFormat rounds that half to '...409.88', one cent above the stored total. Below 2^46 (about 7.04e15 cents) the spacing is under 0.01 and the rounding is exact. Reaching it takes about 7042 largest lines. Fix without a decision: format from integer division and remainder (as priceInputText does) or pass a decimal string to Intl.NumberFormat.format. Shown by arithmetic; not executed here.

confirmed.what_breaks: No test uses a stored id with an uppercase letter, so a planted defect that turns the A-Z range of ID_PATTERN into the characters A, Z and a plus sign survives: a hand-edited document with an id such as Bob1 would be refused as corrupt while a+b would be accepted.

equivalent.why: compareById only breaks a tie between two distinct customers whose ids are unique (shape.js:81 refuses duplicates, deps.newId is a UUID), so a.id === b.id never occurs and <= answers as <; sort reads only the sign.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order is unchanged.
Same as the < mutant: with unique ids the operands are never equal, so > and >= answer the same for every pair the sort passes.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order is unchanged.
The 0 branch is reached only when a.id === b.id, which unique ids rule out for two distinct customers, so the value is never returned.

sumIsExact only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation of the sum, and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.
The line runs only inside if (a.date !== b.date), so the two date strings are never equal and < and <= give the same answer.
hasSafeTotal only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.

The fallback is returned only when ORDER_NUMBER does not match; hasCanonicalNumber then compares order.number with 'ORD-' plus the padded value, which a non-matching string can never equal whatever the value, and hasValidLinks (:86) runs only after every order passed isOrder, so the fallback never decides the result.
